subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact TypeScript module for a static truck model, deciding to skip joints and use fixed dimensions—roughly 7m long, 2.8m wide, with separate wheel parts built directly in model space.

Now I'm designing helper functions for boxes and cylinders, figuring out wheel axle orientation along the X-axis, and settling on a limited cyberpunk palette of gunmetal paint with neon cyan/magenta accents plus hazard-stripe and emblem decals. I'm laying out the chassis, cab, and body sections from back to front along the z-axis.

Writing the cab's extruded side profile...

Working out the rotation angle at 42° to match the slope direction, offsetting it outward slightly, and giving it a dark cyan glow for the visor slit detail. Then I'll move on to the hood armor ramp and the cargo bed container geometry.

Now I'm designing the cargo container hull as a panelled armored box with a wedge-shaped top deck, plus a rooftop missile launcher pod with angled tube clusters, a rear radar dish, and a remote weapon station on the cab roof with a forward-facing barrel.

Computing tube positions...

Working out wheel placement across three axles, with tires sized as dark multi-sided cylinders, glowing neon hub rings, hexagonal metal rims, and armored fender boxes covering each wheel arch.

I'm also planning the greebled details: neon underglow strips, hazard stripes, door decals, headlight/taillight bars, antennas, exhaust stacks, roof light bar, sensor domes, and spike rows, keeping part count manageable within the limit.

Now I'm setting up the builder and sketching out the texture set — a hazard stripe pattern, a neon "ARES-77" tag, a skull-hex emblem, a side screen panel, and grille lines — along with a decal helper for applying them to planes.

Still defining color palette and helper functions...

Adding tread lugs around each tire using a ring pattern, worried the box orientation might not line up correctly with the wheel's local axes, so I'll make the lug shape more symmetric to avoid orientation issues.

Now I'm placing the hub disc, a glowing neon accent ring on the rim, and skipping individual lug nuts for simplicity. I'm adding fender arches above each wheel plus mudflaps, then moving on to the chassis rails.

Now I'm defining the axles, differential pumpkin, and cab details like the bullbar, hazard decal plane, and front bumper box, working out their positions relative to the cab's sloped front face.

Still placing cab features...

Adding the light bar with magenta/cyan glow split, thin roof-corner antennas with glowing tips, and sizing the container box to sit behind the cab with proper gap and height alignment relative to the chassis.

Rear emblem added, then I'm placing rocket pods on the deck at an angle, tilting them upward with a rotation around the x-axis, and working out the tube grid positions within each pod using the perpendicular up vector.

Each pod gets three tubes across and two rows, with a small glowing cylinder at the muzzle end for a red glow effect. Now I'm positioning a radar dish at the rear using a partial sphere geometry tilted to face up and back.

Simplifying to a convex sensor dome plus mast rather than fighting with concave geometry. I'm also placing exhaust stacks behind the cab as cylinders flanking the container, and sketching small equipment boxes beneath for added detail near the wheel positions.

Adding a magenta underglow slab beneath the chassis as a thin glowing box, keeping it narrower than the wheel track so it doesn't clip. I'm noting the front wheel pokes into the cab volume but deciding to skip building a wheel arch cutout for now and leave it simple.

I'll accept the minor tire-cab overlap as visually acceptable, and instead add small fender boxes above each wheel to cover the top intersection cleanly. Then I'm moving to finalize the part composition and sanity-check the cylinder segment counts for the tires sitting flush on the ground.

Checking the lug ring radius against the tire so it doesn't sink below the floor, I'll nudge it down slightly to 0.58 for a near-flush fit, keeping overall vehicle height around 3.4-3.6 with antennas included.

Still writing wheel and bolt geometry...
